title: PostgreSQL psycopg3 search regressions: add numeric filter tests to tests/db/test_workspace_tracking_store.py and run them against a real PostgreSQL
answers: How do I write a regression test for a numeric filter that must work on PostgreSQL with psycopg v3?
Where are the MCP registry timestamp filter database tests?
Why are the PostgreSQL search tests skipped in my local run?
How do I test run attribute filters against the SQL store instead of the in-memory matcher?
body:
Path: tests/db/test_workspace_tracking_store.py exercises SQL search on PostgreSQL with the psycopg v3 driver through the psycopg3_store and psycopg3_registry_store fixtures: run search (test_search_runs_time_filter_binds_integers), MCP registry search over servers, versions and access endpoints (test_search_mcp_registry_time_filters_bind_integers), and dataset and model-version numeric filters.
Rule: When a new numeric attribute reaches SQLAlchemy, add a case here that creates a real row, filters on it with a numeric comparison, and asserts the row comes back; a string bound to an integer column fails at query time, so the assertion catches it. Keep the in-memory matcher checks in tests/utils/test_search_utils.py.
Symptom: none (how-to).
Constraints: These tests need a configured PostgreSQL tracking URI; without it they are collected and skipped locally, so run them in a PostgreSQL-backed environment before relying on them. Fractional-value behavior is not covered by these database tests.
applies: Adding or changing numeric search filters that run through the SQL tracking or registry stores on PostgreSQL.
says: Searching runs by numerical metrics fails with a database query error on Postgres.
Filtering registry servers or versions by timestamp produces a database type mismatch error.
Model version and dataset search filters crash when comparing integer attributes against databases.
Verify that numeric search queries work against actual database engines instead of simulated storage.
Database validation tests for search filters are unexpectedly skipped during local development.
search: When adding or changing numeric search filters for SQL tracking or registry stores on PostgreSQL with psycopg v3, add regression test cases to tests/db/test_workspace_tracking_store.py using the psycopg3_store and psycopg3_registry_store fixtures. The tests must create a real database row, apply a numeric comparison filter, and assert the row is returned, catching query-time failures when strings bind to integer columns across run search, MCP registry searches, datasets, and model versions. Keep in-memory matcher checks in tests/utils/test_search_utils.py; these database tests require a configured PostgreSQL tracking URI, are skipped locally without one, and do not cover fractional-value behavior.
